title: Transpose Stamp Correspondence
question: The black-bordered mini-grid is the reference. Swap its rows and columns: the cell at row r, column c moves to row c, column r. Exactly one colored-bordered mini-grid is the result. Which border color marks it? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

task_signature.mechanism: Transpose a binary cell-incidence matrix, compare it with three equal-ink candidates, and return the matched candidate's border attribute.

latent_z.description: A movable compact plaque with one binary reference grid, three candidate grids, a permutation of answer-color bindings, and its visible anchor.

latent_alias.justification: Every declared scene field changes rendered pixels, and the sampled nonsymmetric reference plus ordered colored candidate panels has no intended pixel-identical reparameterization.

boundary.observable: The decision boundary is exact visible cell agreement after row-column exchange; every wrong candidate visibly differs in at least two cells.
boundary.quarantine: Quarantine any scene without one unique exact transpose match or with a runner-up Hamming distance below two cells.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Unlike Quarter-Turn Atlas, it matches neither disconnected landmarks nor rigid rotations; unlike Ribbon Link, it transfers no adjacency edge; unlike Woven Necklace, it has no cyclic equivalence; unlike Difference Mosaic, it applies no Boolean operation to paired masks; and unlike Shuffle Echo, it does not transfer a shape's original slot. It tests row-column incidence correspondence inside one inspection plaque.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: It isolates whether a model can bind discrete row and column roles through matrix transposition before reporting an independently permuted color attribute.
